def: A habitual or unscheduled pattern of absence from workplace duties without authorized leave or prior notice.
Salary owed for a past period, paid later — for example after a back-dated increment.
Correcting a missed or wrong punch with a reason, usually approved by HR.
The fixed core part of pay. PF, gratuity and often HRA are worked out from it.

A performance appraisal method based on forced distribution, where a fixed percentage of employees must be ranked into predetermined rating bands (such as 10% top, 20% above, 40% middle, 20% below, and 10% bottom).
A file in your bank's format listing each employee's account and net pay for bulk transfer.
Unused leave moved into the next leave year, often up to a limit.
Cost to Company — everything the employer spends on an employee in a year, including employer PF.
Dearness Allowance, paid to offset inflation; counted with basic for PF and gratuity where paid.
Amounts subtracted from gross pay, such as PF, ESI, professional tax, TDS and loan recovery.
Amounts the employer pays on top of salary, such as employer PF and ESI.
Employees' Provident Fund. Employee and employer each contribute 12% of basic (commonly capped at ₹15,000).
Employees' State Insurance for staff earning up to ₹21,000 gross a month: 0.75% employee, 3.25% employer.
The last payment to a leaving employee: pending salary, leave encashment, gratuity, minus recoveries.
Minutes after shift start during which a check-in is still treated as on time.
A lump sum after 5+ years of service: 15/26 × last basic + DA × years of service.
Total earnings before deductions.
A day where the employee worked less than the full-day threshold but more than the minimum.
House Rent Allowance, part of salary meant for rent; partly tax-exempt under the old regime.
Paying unused leave in cash, usually at exit or year end.
Loss of Pay — days without pay, reducing the month's salary.
Take-home pay after all deductions.
Steps to bring a new employee in: records, documents, access and equipment.
Hours worked beyond the normal schedule, often paid at a higher rate.
Days in the month the employee is paid for: present days, paid leave, holidays and weekly offs.
The process of calculating, approving and paying salaries for a period.
A statement of one employee's earnings, deductions and net pay for a month.
A state tax on employment, deducted monthly; amount depends on the state.
A schedule showing which employee works which shift on which day.
A defined block of working hours, with start, end, breaks and weekly offs.
Tax Deducted at Source — income tax deducted from salary each month.
Days not paid: absence without approved leave or unpaid leave.
Universal Account Number — an employee's lifelong PF account number.
The regular day(s) off each week, such as Sunday.
